newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures steady after stream of Buba comments.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures steady after stream of Buba comments.

text.p: German Bund futures were unchanged in late trade after spending the day shrugging off a steady stream of economic data and comments from top Bundesbank officials.

The DTB Bund future was down two basis points in late trade at 99.33 after having traded in a range between 99.10 and 99.40 during the day, almost exactly what traders had forecast at the start of dealings this morning.
"There was a lot news today, but at the end of the day it did not amount to much new information for the market," said one analyst at a Frankfurt bank.
Bundesbank officials, who have offered at times conflicting remarks about the direction of interest rates, today seemed to indicate that there is room to cut rates if the economy eases.

But bond market traders took no chances and continued to act as if rates will not be cut, especially after the six leading economic institutes forecast 1.5 percent German growth this year and 2.5 percent next.
The spread between two and five year notes narrowed to 114.5 percent from 119.4 percent the day before.
Bunds were supported late in the day by a stronger Treasury market, but German debt underperformed its U.S. counterpart.
The T-note/Bund spread narrowed to 53 basis points from 63 basis points after the release of the U.S. Employment Cost Index this afternoon.
Traders said that Bunds recent weakness leaves the market clearly negative, but that the 99.02 level should hold any sell-off because it is the low point of trading the last three- and-a-half weeks.
